messages:
maria (devex): FYI our example app fails when run in the edge runtime bundle — works fine in node. stack trace shows \"Unexpected token 'export'\" on an internal module import. anyone seen pnpm/monorepo + exports play weird with edge builds?
ryan (eng-runtime): ugh yup. usually means the bundler resolved the CJS entry or a file that hasn't been transpiled to ESM. are we shipping both cjs+esm in that package?
sam (pkg-maintainer): package publishes dist/cjs and dist/esm. package.json has \"main\" -> dist/cjs/index.js and \"module\" -> dist/esm/index.js and an \"exports\" field but not fully covering subpaths. pnpm hoists by content-addressed symlink layout, maybe the edge optimizer picks the wrong resolution.
jade (ts): can you paste the package's exports block?
maria (devex): sure, snippet below (redacted):
```json
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./*": "./dist/cjs/*",
  ".": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
}
```
ryan (eng-runtime): there — exports only points to cjs. most bundlers will pick the first matching export for an import specifier, and if they don't see an \"import\" conditional they'll fall back to whatever exists. edge runtime expects ESM.
sam (pkg-maintainer): oof, that was a lazy copy-over. we forgot conditional exports. quick patch idea: add an explicit import/require mapping so ESM consumers get the esm build.
jade (ts): right, change to something like:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
ryan (eng-runtime): also double-check that the published tarball actually contains dist/esm. pnpm workspace symlinks can mask publish-time mistakes because local dev works but install from registry will fail in CI/bundler.
maria (devex): confirmed dist/esm was excluded by mistake (ignore list). fixing and republishing now. aside: is there anything we can do in the app bundler to be more resilient?
ryan (eng-runtime): if you control the app build, ensure the optimizer respects \"exports\" conditionals and target environment. For Vercel/edge, set target to node-like ESM or force resolution to the package's \"import\" entry. In webpack/rollup, prefer resolutionMainFields: ['exports','module','main'] or use resolve.exportsFields.
sam (pkg-maintainer): for monorepo folks — avoid \"./*": "./dist/cjs/*" style that overrides subpath exports. it prevents conditional exports from matching. and add a ./package.json entry so tools can inspect the correct metadata.
jade (ts): typing gotchas: if types field points at types/index.d.ts but your build outputs types under dist/esm/types, TS server in a workspace may resolve the symlinked path differently. best practice: set \"types\" to the same surfaced entry that consumers import (e.g., dist/esm/index.d.ts) and include it in files array.
maria (devex): thanks — republished with exports fixed and types entry updated. redeploying edge sample now.
build-bot: deploy started for branch fix/es-exports (build 8942) :rocket:
ryan (eng-runtime): one more note — if anyone hits \"module not found\" from a symlinked dependency in pnpm, try setting pnpm config \"public-hoist-pattern[]\" or use \"pnpm install --shamefully-hoist\" as a last resort, but prefer fixing exports.
maria (devex): deployed, edge sample is green. adding a PR template checklist to avoid this for future packages: include esm build, conditional exports, package.json types, and verify tarball contents.
sam (pkg-maintainer): will add a prepublish check script that verifies exports conditionals exist and dist has both targets. thanks for catching this fast :pray: 
jade (ts): happy path — if someone wants a quick grep to find offending packages in the monorepo:
```bash
rg "\"\.\": \"./dist/cjs" --glob '!node_modules' || true
```
maria (devex): perfect. closing this thread but leaving notes in the sample-app README. :white_check_mark:
